newsitem.title: CANADA: Asian demand, Argentine rains buoy wheat price - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Asian demand, Argentine rains buoy wheat price - CWB.

text.p: Heavy Argentine rains as well as Indian and Iranian wheat purchases have raised world prices on mid-grade wheat, a Canadian Wheat Board analyst said.
"The harvest problems in Argentina have rallied prices. They've had quite a bit of rain in their southern region where they produce up to 60 percent of their crop," CWB analyst Larry Sawatzky said.
"Reports indicated up to one million tonnes of Argentina's wheat crop could be either lost or damaged," he said.
The CWB on Thursday raised its world wheat price forecast for mid-grade wheat by C$4 to C$5 a tonne.
Benchmark high-grade No1 Canada Western Red Spring wheat remained unchanged, however, at C$194-C$214 a tonne.
But No3 CWRS increased C$4 a tonne to the C$183-C$203 a tonne range compared with November's CWB price forecast.

"There is steady import demand over the past month with India said they're importing two million tonnes," Sawatzky said. "That was a big surprise, and we're seeing strong demand from Iran. They're expected to import quite a bit more than they did last year."
